purpose: Per-segment flexion/extension caps for the synthetic flexion-extension cine (tools/polypose/cine_render.py). A frame's segment angle is frac * m * (a_k * ext if a_k > 0 else a_k * flex) with a_k = -sin(2 pi k / N); lateral bending and axial rotation are held at 0.
conventions: flex = lordosis-reducing, ext = lordosis-increasing, one direction each, degrees from the neutral pose (the spec's own convention, copied with its rows). A row is usable only when it carries numeric flex and ext and no 'pending' status. cine_render.py REFUSES to plan a region any of whose moving segments is pending or absent: no number is invented, interpolated or borrowed from a neighbouring segment.

copied_from.sha256_of: the file as committed at `commit`, LF line endings: `git show <commit>:<path> | sha256sum`. A Windows working tree with core.autocrlf=true hashes the same commit as 192c264ba22fd888ee1f90cefca230b493184c998f9ef80c1531aa3235615838 (CRLF), which is what this field wrongly held until 2026-09-26; cine_render.load_rom compares it with CRLF normalised to LF (spec_is_copied_version), as a record only -- the rows are the refusal
copied_from.rule: rows and citations copied verbatim, source keys included; cine_render.py refuses to plan if any copied row no longer equals the spec's row (drift)

note: Hard caps on the relative rotation of one segment, per direction, from the neutral supine pose. flex = lordosis-reducing, ext = lordosis-increasing, lb and ar are one-side values. Source per row. Values are in vitro at 7.5-10 N m; in vivo totals (Pearcy 1984) are ~14 deg per lumbar joint, i.e. the in vitro flex+ext sums (10.1-17.8) bracket them.

T10-T11.note: n=6 at +/-7.5 N m; means of the per-specimen rows of S1 Dataset (pone.0177823.s001.xlsx): flex = ROM+, ext = |ROM-|, lb and ar = mean of the two measured sides; sd = sample SD (n-1). Corrected 2026-09-26 from 1.75/1.75/2.1/2.4, which treated per-direction values as two-direction totals and halved them.

oxland1992.ref: Oxland TR, Lin RM, Panjabi MM. Three-dimensional mechanical properties of the thoracolumbar junction. J Orthop Res 1992;10(4):573-580.
oxland1992.design: in vitro, n=11 T11-L1 three-vertebra specimens, 7.5 N m, ROM to one side, mean +/- SD
oxland1992.verified: abstract read verbatim 2026-09-23; both segments' four-direction values with SDs re-confirmed verbatim from the PubMed efetch abstract the same day (T11-T12 2.7/2.4/3.5/1.8, T12-L1 2.9/3.9/3.7/1.2)

pearcy1984a.ref: Pearcy M, Portek I, Shepherd J. Three-dimensional x-ray analysis of normal movement in the lumbar spine. Spine 1984;9(3):294-297.
pearcy1984a.design: in vivo biplanar radiography, asymptomatic volunteers: each lumbar joint ~14 deg total flexion+extension, lower levels slightly more

pearcy1984b.ref: Pearcy MJ, Tibrewal SB. Axial rotation and lateral bending in the normal lumbar spine measured by three-dimensional radiography. Spine 1984;9(6):582-587.
pearcy1984b.design: in vivo: ~2 deg axial rotation per joint (L3-4, L4-5 slightly more); lateral bending ~10 deg at the upper three levels, 6 deg L4-5, 3 deg L5-S1

wilke2017.ref: Wilke HJ, Herkommer A, Werner K, Liebsch C. In vitro analysis of the segmental flexibility of the thoracic spine. PLoS One 2017;12(5):e0177823.
wilke2017.design: in vitro, n=6-7 per level, +/-7.5 N m pure moments, monosegmental FSUs T1-T2 to T11-T12 with the costovertebral joints kept and no rib cage; ROM reported per direction (ROM+ and ROM- columns in S1)
wilke2017.verified: citation, PMID and DOI confirmed 2026-09-23 (PubMed). 2026-09-26: rom_deg T10-T11 recomputed from the per-specimen rows of S1 Dataset (pone.0177823.s001.xlsx), reproducing its Mean rows; two independent extractions agree to 0.01 deg. The Results bands (e.g. 'ranged from 3.1 to 3.8') are per-direction values, not two-direction totals

yamamoto1989.ref: Yamamoto I, Panjabi MM, Crisco T, Oxland T. Three-dimensional movements of the whole lumbar spine and lumbosacral joint. Spine 1989;14(11):1256-1260.
yamamoto1989.design: in vitro, n=10 fresh cadaveric L1-sacrum, pure moments to 10 N m, ROM per direction (axial torque and lateral bending to one side)
yamamoto1989.verified: abstract read verbatim 2026-09-23 (Europe PMC); all five segments' flexion / extension / lateral-bending / axial-torque values re-confirmed verbatim from the PubMed efetch abstract the same day (L1-2 5.8/4.3/4.9/2.3 ... L5-S1 10.0/7.8/5.5/1.4)
